questions.answer: Cricket, above all, which is almost a national obsession here. I enjoy playing casually, but I love watching it even more. I also play a bit of badminton, which is a fun way to stay [[active]] with friends.

questions.q: Did you play much sport as a child?
questions.answer: All the time. After school, my friends and I would play cricket in any open field we could find, often until it got dark. Those [[makeshift]] matches, with a taped tennis ball and a wooden bat, are some of my happiest memories.

Absolutely, especially cricket. There's a real buzz when the national team is playing, and the whole country seems to stop and watch. Even people who aren't usually into sport get [[caught up]] in the excitement.

questions.q: Is there a sport you would like to try in the future?
questions.answer: I'd love to learn to swim properly, which might sound surprising given that I grew up beside a huge river. I can just about stay afloat, but I'd like to improve, partly for fitness and partly because it's such a [[vital life skill]].

questions.q: Do you think sport is important for young people?
questions.answer: Definitely. Beyond keeping them fit, sport teaches young people how to cope with losing, cooperate with others and stay disciplined. At a time when so many kids are [[glued to their screens]], getting them outside matters more than ever.
